a: A clear mind, free of limiting assumptions, where less achieves more
A schedule with fewer tasks and more free time each day
A routine that removes all difficult work from a project
A mindset that treats rest as more important than results
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes the Effortless State as a mind cleared of assumptions and negative thoughts, where you do less but achieve more.

questions.q: What is a Minimum Viable Action?
a: The smallest obvious step toward your goal
The quickest way to finish an entire project
The least valuable task on your to-do list
The first draft of a finished product
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to break work into chunks, find the smallest obvious step, and then do just that.

questions.q: Why does McKeown say you should share bad ideas?
a: Imperfect ideas can start a successful process
Bad ideas help you appreciate the good ones
Sharing them proves you are not a perfectionist
Other people will improve them for you
questions.why: Lesson 3 says allowing imperfect products and unfinished ideas makes it easier to learn from failure and build something successful.

questions.q: What work rhythm does the summary recommend?
a: Focused sessions of about 90 minutes with short breaks
Long days of work followed by a full week off
Many short tasks switched every few minutes
One continuous block until the work is finished
questions.why: Lesson 1 suggests focusing effort in a session of about 90 minutes with short breaks, since the brain cannot perform at its peak all day.

questions.q: How should you pace a long project?
a: Spread your energy evenly instead of burning out early
Work as hard as possible at the start to gain a lead
Save all the work for a final burst of effort
Alternate between total effort and total rest
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to distribute resources evenly and store energy for the whole period rather than exhausting yourself at the beginning.
